extracted.intended_audience: NIH K99/R00 reviewers, mentors, and grant-panel readers
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted criteria relate to experimental rigor, validation, reproducibility, responsible conduct of research training, and mentor/co-mentor plans described in a K99/R00 grant application. Includes statistical, sample-size, blinding, training, and transition-to-independence expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blinding of qualitative measurements
rubrics_metrics.description: All qualitative measurements, including lifespans and microscopy, will be double-blinded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement double-blind procedures for qualitative endpoints to reduce observer bias. (Page: 'All qualitative measurements, including lifespans and microscopy, will be double-blinded.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Random assignment of animals and samples
rubrics_metrics.description: All animals and samples will be assigned at random.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use randomization procedures for allocation of animals/samples to conditions to prevent selection bias; document methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of replicates and sample sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: All replicates and sample sizes will be provided for all analyses to provide transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report number of replicates and per-replicate sample sizes for each analysis. Examples in text: sample sizes ranging from 43–234 cells per replicate; plan for n > 200 cells per condition in human cells.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple independent approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: All questions will be interrogated using multiple independent approaches to ensure against biases of a single method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine orthogonal methods (e.g., biochemical assays, genetic perturbations, imaging, proteomics) so conclusions do not rely on a single technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Run-to-run variability check using Kruskal-Wallis
rubrics_metrics.description: Run samples to ensure >5 replicates show nonsignificant differences using Kruskal-Wallis testing for each mutant tested to ensure that run-to-run variability/noise is insignificant compared to strain-to-strain differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform Kruskal-Wallis (or appropriate nonparametric) tests across technical/biological replicates; require >5 replicates with nonsignificant differences to accept low run-to-run variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation with pharmacological controls
rubrics_metrics.description: To validate the assay, test cells treated with actin stabilizing drugs (jasplakinolide) to increase F:G actin ratios, and actin-destabilizing drugs (latrunculinA) to decrease F:G actin ratios.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include positive/negative pharmacological controls to show assay sensitivity to expected perturbations; corroborate with genetic perturbations (shRNA/CRISPR lines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Genetic perturbation validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Test conservation of candidate genes (BRD4, KAT5, HNF4, HSF1 homologues) by knockdown/knockout and measure effects on F:G actin ratios.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use available shRNA and CRISPR-knockout lines; expect specific directional changes (e.g., knockdown of BRD4/KAT5/HNF4/HSF1 should result in decreased F:G actin ratios if hypotheses hold).

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing preparation-artifact caveat (trypsinization)
rubrics_metrics.description: CAVEAT: trypsinization to move adherent cells into microwells may cause significant changes to cytoskeletal structures, introducing artifacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mitigation strategies: 1) use suspension Jurkat cell lines to determine whether trypsinization produces irreproducible artifacts; 2) develop on-chip culturing and lysis (ECM-coated polyacrylamide gels and polyacrylamide gel microwell arrays) to avoid harmful preparation steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-system adaptation and validation (C. elegans)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adapt scWB system into C. elegans using single-cells isolated by established protocols and FACS (LifeAct::mRuby lines) to perform tissue-specific studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advantages: reuse microwell arrays, enable tissue-specific assays; plan to verify assay detects age-related shift away from F-actin towards G-actin across cell types and ages (D1, D4, D7, D10) using >100 cells and same statistical rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum sample-size targets for assays
rubrics_metrics.description: Human cell experiments: n > 200 cells per condition. C. elegans scWB sampling: use >100 cells per timepoint/cell type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure sufficient per-condition cell counts to support statistical comparisons; combine with replicate-level reproducibility checks (>5 replicates nonsignificant) as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated separation and quantification of F and G actin
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrated ability to separate F:G actin species in both MDM-MBA-231 and BJ fibroblast cell lines and robustly quantify F and G actin using standard actin antibodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide empirical evidence (e.g., data from >22 replicates, per-replicate cell counts) showing reliable separation/quantification as part of assay validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical reporting and interpretation (non-significant differences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report statistical tests used (e.g., Kruskal-Wallis) and interpret nonsignificant differences across replicates as evidence that run-to-run variability is minor relative to biological differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify choice of tests, justify nonparametric versus parametric, and explicitly relate statistical outcomes to assay reliability and biological inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR) training format
rubrics_metrics.description: Format: formal training with five face-to-face class meetings going over NIH RCR requirements, plus informal training in the lab and online CITI curriculum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary RCR training: five face-to-face meetings (minimally two hours each). Informal instruction throughout fellowship via lab interactions and weekly meetings. Use online CITI modules; plan to retake course if awarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR subject-matter coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: RCR topics to be covered: (a) conflict of interest; (b) ethical use of animals; (c) history of humans and research; (d) data management and access to research tools; (e) responsible conduct of research; (f) mentorship; (g) authorship and publication; (h) stem cell research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure each enumerated RCR topic is explicitly addressed during formal and informal training sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR faculty participation and frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Training faculty (principal investigator Dr. Andrew Dillin) will participate directly in the training; online modules taken minimally twice monthly to solidify learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PI/faculty should be actively engaged in RCR teaching; schedule periodic online refreshers and embed RCR discussion into lab activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor/co-mentor formal meeting cadence
rubrics_metrics.description: During the K99 phase, Ryo will meet with the advisory committee every 6 months to discuss research progress; formal one-on-one meetings with mentor are monthly; presentations in lab meetings every six months; informal meetings occur every few days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a documented schedule of advisory and one-on-one meetings to monitor progress, provide feedback, and prepare for transition to independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in teaching and mentoring responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide opportunities to mentor students and to teach: assign new students to mentee, let them act as TA in lectures and labs, help develop laboratory manual and course materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give mentee progressive responsibilities (undergrads, rotation students, grad students) and structured feedback; monthly meetings with lab manager to develop management skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition-to-independence plan and assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: At culmination of Year 1, assess whether the candidate is prepared for faculty search; mentor will assist with applications, interviews, negotiation, and staff/equipment acquisition during R00 phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal checkpoints (6-month advisory meetings, Year 1 assessment), mentor involvement in career-development activities, and practical negotiation/training support (lab manager aiding equipment negotiation and hiring).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship and data access / data portability commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Data collected for the screen and any data generated during the K99 portion can be brought to the candidate's own laboratory when they acquire a faculty position; future publications from this work will be his and he will be senior author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document commitments regarding ownership/portability of data and authorship expectations to avoid later conflicts; maintain open dialogue to avoid competitive overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of collaborative core expertise and cross-training
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidate will train with collaborators and cores (e.g., experts in RNA-seq/ATAC-seq/ChIP-seq, single-cell immunoblot, proteomics, biophysics) to gain necessary skills and access resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan explicit cross-training visits and collaborations (weeks in collaborator labs, use of cores) to acquire analytical and technical skills needed for proposed aims.
